newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden Shareholders positive to Swedish bank merge.
newsitem.headline: Sweden Shareholders positive to Swedish bank merge.

text.p: Sweden's Shareholders' Association said on Tuesday it was positive to the proposed merger between Swedbank and Foreningsbanken.
"The proposed deal benefits both Foreningsbanken's and Swedbank's shareholders," the group said in a statement.
"The Shareholders' Association has ... attached large importance to the fact that two competent and independant boards unanimously have recommended the deal," it said.
The group called for compulsory redemption of possible outstanding Foreningsbanken shares to avoid costly future court cases for the new bank.
Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced plans to merger in February.
Under the arrangement Foreningsbanken shareholders can swap seven A-series shares for two shares in the new bank, called ForeningsSparbanken, and three preference shares for one newly-issued share.
The acceptance period runs from April 15 to May 15 and the new bank is expected to start operations on January 1, 1998.
The merger prospectus was issued last week.
